status: merged (user-verified 2026-10-15) as 098e627827; fix2 (rim side selectable + Place-on-face gated to bore) merged as 61f46aabff, user-verified; fix3 (teardrop horizontal-only, Custom sizes, Head/Fit highlight) merged as 030e512e89, user-verified; screw-teardrop (teardrop a screw's clearance bore, optional head on the same row, shared apex) merged as be3367cdeb, user-verified; fix4 (round features under a non-uniform instance scale; only bore/pocket stays world-round - teardrop/rim/fill object-space, nut fill fixed) merged as 9df5069703, user-verified 2026-10-16; chamfer-fillet (Rim chamfer/fillet merged into one Chamfer/Fillet op + Both ends checkbox) merged as 1ef89702db, user-verified 2026-10-16
notes: Detects cylindrical walls and applies one operation volume per hole: teardrop (horizontal only), bore/pocket (screw / insert / magnet / nut / custom), rim chamfer / fillet; bore/pocket also authorable on any flat face. Shrinking adds a positive annulus (its_make_shrink_tube) whose caps land exactly on the detected wall's ends, so it comes out flush with the faces the hole was bored through. No keys, no CAD. See notes/ME-2.md. FIX2 (2026-10-15, patch 32_ME-2-fix2.patch): the rim chamfer/fillet had no Flip (entry) control - it rendered inside the bore branch only - so on a detected hole (axis sign ignores the material) the ring was stuck on one mouth; Flip now renders for bore and rim (a teardrop is centred on the hole and ignores the entry). Place on face, which stamped the current operation's shape onto a bare face, now shows only for bore/pocket: set_place_face_mode refuses it for other operations and set_operation exits the mode when leaving bore. FIX3 (2026-10-15, patch 33_ME-2-fix3.patch): teardrop now offers horizontal holes only (a hole_usable() gate on the previews, hover and count; a near-vertical detected axis previously built a teardrop ghost with a garbage up direction). The standard combo gained a Custom entry and is_screw/is_nut/is_pocket now derive from the category, so editing the diameter to a non-catalogue size no longer shows M2/M3 or turns a nut into a circle; the standalone Custom category button is removed (size-only Custom: no screw head styles, no nut clearance bore). Head and Fit buttons now highlight the active choice. FEAT (2026-10-15, patch 34_ME-2-teardrop.patch): bore/pocket Screw gets a Teardrop checkbox (shaft only by default), a Teardrop-head checkbox for a counterbore, sharing the Teardrop operation's apex angle. New libslic3r its_make_teardrop_prism generalizes its_make_teardrop_for_hole onto any axis; a vertical hole falls back to round. FIX4 (2026-10-15, patch 35_ME-2-scale.patch): features are built in world space and pulled back through instance_matrix().inverse(), so a non-uniform instance scale no longer flattens them into ellipses (the ME-2d object_scale division only held for a uniform scale). Rim/shrink radii from an elliptical hole stay approximate. FIX5 (2026-10-16, patch 37_ME-2-chamfer-fillet.patch): the two rim operations are merged into one Chamfer/Fillet op (Teardrop | Bore/Pocket | Chamfer/Fillet) with a Chamfer|Fillet toggle (default chamfer), a size field and a Both ends checkbox that rims both mouths of a through hole; Flip hides when Both ends is on. Volume names unchanged. FIX4b (2026-10-16, patch 36_ME-2-fill.patch): only bore/pocket is built round-in-world (teardrop/rim follow the hole's own edge in object space again), and the shrink fill is object space so it fills the stretched wall exactly and now covers nuts too (inner wall inside the world-round bore's object ellipse). SYNC (2026-10-15): HoleStandards adopted upstream OrcaSlicer's hole table so the CAD Hole feature and this tool keep one source of truth - new cbore_d/cbore_depth/csink_pocket_d seat columns, UNC designations with a bare-size lookup ("1/4-20" -> "1/4-20 UNC"), the #10-24 UNC size, and 82 deg inch flat-head seats; CadDocument::add_hole_standard() consumes the seat columns instead of the head dimensions. The inch sizes this tool offers therefore move to upstream's ASME values (metric head dimensions unchanged).

title: Alt pivot snap in the Move gizmo
notes: Dragging a Move grabber with Alt held runs ObjectSnap::hit_under_cursor over the non-moving volumes and overrides the axis displacement so the pivot reaches the target coordinate; the gizmo is a one-axis drag, so the snap keeps that constraint and slides the object along the dragged axis. Its markers use the unbracketed "// ORCAPORT:" comment form, which is why the row was missing. Row added late.

title: Fill from above (inside the Cut gizmo)
config_keys: (none; reuses the cut plane plus a "Lower by" offset)
notes: Reproduces the manual cut / duplicate / lower workflow: keep the half above the cut plane, keep the slab 0..d above it, drop that slab by d, and add it as a positive MODEL_PART volume named FillFromAbove#<n>. On a prismatic wall the lowered band is the un-engraved surface exactly, so the recess fills by construction rather than by approximation. No [ORCAPORT:HF-2] marker - plain "// HF-2" comments in GLGizmoCut.*; the kernel is CutUtils::fill_from_above_mesh. Deliberate ceiling: the band is the full cross-section at that height, so it can spill inside a hollow part and the user trims it. Row added late.

title: Support transition layers (interface/base)
config_keys: (none; signalled by a ";SU8_FAN <percent>" G-code marker the generator emits)
notes: Tags the layers where support interface meets base material or the object (1 = interface-on-base, 2 = object-on-interface), emits the transition-layer temperature delta once per layer at the toolchange, forces a part-cooling fan for that layer, and applies a relative transition-layer slowdown. Part of the woven support-interface family (SU-9/10/11/13); its keys are tagged [ORCAPORT:SU-9]. NOT present in Neotko's fork: SupportCommon.cpp carries no NEOTKO tag and the fork has no support_interface_weave* keys.

title: Woven support interface
notes: Splits each woven interface layer into alternating strips of support-base and interface material along an angle (split_weave_strips), giving each connected component an even number of strips (>= 2) derived from its width so narrow spans still interlock. Only interface layers are woven - the contact is never woven, and the top two layers of a stack stay solid so a woven layer is never adjacent to the object. weave_layers sets how many layers are woven, weave_pitch the strip pitch, weave_flush lowers the base thread of the woven layers so the top sits flush. Inert at defaults. This key family is the group tag for SU-8/10/11/13.

title: Support contact interface line width
notes: Overrides the contact interface line width separately for top and bottom contact; the value honours mm or % of the nozzle, and the fill spacing is matched to the overridden width so the contact layer stays closed. Inert at 0 (default).

title: Support interface loop / boustrophedon
notes: Emits the interface as a boustrophedon along a strip's long axis plus a closed perimeter loop around the region, so an interface layer has long continuous paths instead of many short per-line starts. Lines are ordered from the side nearest the region centre to the far side. Reuses the upstream support_interface_loop_pattern key.

title: Support bottom-stack weave and flush
notes: Bottom contact stack: a base-material layer projected from a bottom contact is the weave host, the interface layer above it is woven, and a solid base-material cap is inserted between the weave and the base so the bottom stack interlocks. Flush widens that solid base-interface layer to 1.25x the nozzle so the top comes out level. Inert at defaults.
